newsitem.title: USA: Calif. sends electricity ISO plans to FERC.
newsitem.headline: Calif. sends electricity ISO plans to FERC.

text.p: Plans for how California will implement an independent system operator (ISO) and power exchange for its restructured electricity industry were submitted Monday to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in Washington DC.
In a statement, Southern California Edison Co said the filings keep the state on track to introduce competition into the market next year.
Last November, FERC had conditionally approved joint recommendations from Edison, Pacific Gas & Electric Co and San Diego Gas and Electric Co on the creation of an ISO and power exchange.

Monday's filings add details to those plans and include an agreement that tranmission owners will have an obligation to build transmission that the ISO decides is needed for economy or reliability, Edison said.
The latest filings also stipulate that transmission congestion contracts will not be implemented at this time, but will be evaluated by the ISO governing board.
A proposal was also included to limit the horizontal market power of large out-of-state sellers such as the Bonneville Power Administration in the California market.
